subject: A/B rollout safety criteria and conditional SLA carveout request
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novafin.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: A/B rollout with pinned fallback & SLA carveout

Irene —

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. As discussed, NovaFin is preparing to deploy the new embedding+rerank path for our search feature. Because of the increased request fanout and our strict p95 latency targets for real-time search, we want to run an A/B-style rollout but need guarantees that we can fall back quickly if latency or error rate regresses.

Specifically, we are asking Redwood for:
- a formal playbook for a staged A/B rollout (traffic ramps, monitoring windows)
- an automatic fallback/pinning option so traffic can be switched to a pinned stable model (or prior version) without manual intervention
- a temporary SLA carveout (or credit arrangement) while we run the canary and stabilize, in case we see transient SLO misses during the ramp window

Attached is our Q1 latency report showing spikes during long tails (latency-report-q1.pdf). Our timeline: start canary next Wed (2027-04-28), run for up to 72 hours with staged ramps.

Can you confirm Redwood’s tolerance for the following conditions and the exact rollback triggers you will adopt? If we can get a short written agreement (even a 1–2 paragraph addendum) we can proceed with Ops scheduling and our change board approval.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Turner
Platform Engineering, NovaFin
ops@novafin.com

--
Attachment: latency-report-q1.pdf (report, 1.2MB)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novafin.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: A/B rollout with pinned fallback & SLA carveout

Alex —

Appreciate the detail and the report. I’ve sketched a proposed rollout + mitigation plan and am looping in Sales, SRE and CS so we can agree to thresholds and approvals before your change window. See attached playbook (proposed-rollout-playbook.md). Highlights:

- Canary plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% (progression windows 30/60/120 mins respectively, subject to metrics)
- Monitoring: rolling 5-minute windows, evaluate p95 latency, p99 tail, and 5xx rate
- Initial rollback triggers (proposed): if p95 > 300ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows OR 5xx rate > 2% in a 5-minute window -> automatic fallback to pinned version (v1.2-stable)
- Pinning mechanism: route traffic through a policy that can atomically redirect to a pinned model variant; fallback should complete within <30s of trigger
- Safety net: canary will run behind a circuit-breaker that restricts concurrency and enforces per-customer rate limits

Request to Redwood leadership: temporary SLA carveout for the canary window (72 hours max) such that transient SLO misses during the ramp do not trigger standard SLA credit calculations, provided the rollout follows the above playbook and automatic fallback rules. We’ll document an MAP and a short addendum for signatures.

Next steps for internal owners: Aditya — commercial acceptance and any credit/contract language. Rishi — confirm technical thresholds and rollback implementation. Grace — CS to coordinate NovaFin’s change board and pre-notify their on-call. Alex, if the above looks close I’ll push a formal MAP and we’ll schedule a brief approval call.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Account Success — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0133

--
Attachment: proposed-rollout-playbook.md (markdown, 6 KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@novafin.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: A/B rollout with pinned fallback & SLA carveout

Irene —

This direction makes sense from a commercial standpoint. A couple of notes:
- We should be explicit about credit mechanics in the MAP: if the canary triggers an automatic fallback and the fallback prevents an outage, we still want to preserve the carveout (no credits) provided the playbook executed correctly. If the rollback fails and customers saw sustained SLO breaches beyond the playbook window, credit rules should apply.
- Recommend adding an acceptance gate: signoff from Head of Reliability (Rishi) + CS confirmation that NovaFin’s change board has approved the schedule.

If Rishi confirms the exact numeric thresholds and ops runbook, I’ll prepare the MAP and the short contract addendum to waive credit calculations during the defined ramp window. Alex — if you can confirm your change board date/time we’ll lock the start.

-Aditya
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novafin.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: A/B rollout with pinned fallback & SLA carveout

Irene/Aditya —

Thanks for pulling this together. From the reliability side I can approve a conditional SLA carveout for the 72-hour canary window provided we adopt stricter, machine-observable triggers and an automated rollback path. I propose the following concrete edits to the playbook:

- Monitoring windows: evaluate 1-minute and 5-minute rolling windows (we need 1-min for fast detection)
- Rollback triggers (final):
  * p95 latency > 250ms sustained for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows OR
  * p99 latency increase > 30% vs. baseline in a 5-minute window OR
  * 5xx rate >= 1% in any 1-minute window
- Action: automatic fallback to pinned model (v1.2-stable) executed by routing policy; the switch must be atomic and complete within 20s.
- Observation: after fallback, a 15-minute stabilization window where traffic remains on pinned model while post-mortem metrics are collected. Only after a joint ops review can we unstuck and re-attempt a roll.
- Instrumentation: require synthetic probe checks and an internal health endpoint. Canary abort must emit an event to PagerDuty and create a SUP ticket (SUP-2248).

If these are acceptable to NovaFin, we will sign a brief MAP and addendum that waives credit calculations during the defined window, conditional on following the playbook and the automated fallback. If the playbook wasn’t followed or fallback failed to execute, normal SLA credit rules will apply.

Grace — please confirm you’ve informed NovaFin’s change board and will be the CS approver on the MAP. Alex — please confirm the canary start date/time so SRE can schedule a watch rotation.

I’m copying the internal runbook in the SUP ticket and will post the final MAP link once Aditya gives the green light.

-Rishi
Senior Director, Reliability Engineering — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
